scenarios.text:
CASE STUDY: Contoso Platform Team

Contoso is moving an internal application to GitHub. The team wants a clean repository structure, protected collaboration on feature branches, and a repeatable review process before merging changes into the main branch.

CASE STUDY: Fabrikam DevOps Modernization

Fabrikam manages several services in GitHub and wants automation for build validation, a consistent way to track work, and clear visibility into issues and pull requests across multiple teams.

CASE STUDY: Northwind Open Source Program

Northwind is publishing a public project on GitHub. The maintainers need help onboarding contributors, managing community discussions, protecting sensitive settings, and organizing work across an organization.

questions.Question: Which statement best describes Git?

Options.text: A distributed version control system used to track changes and coordinate work.
Options.reason: Git is a distributed version control system.

Options.text: A code hosting service without local history.
A build service for compiling apps.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Git stores project history locally and supports branching, merging, and collaboration.

questions.Question: What is the main purpose of cloning a repository?

Options.text: To create a new branch on GitHub.
To create a local copy of a remote repository.
Options.reason: Cloning copies a remote repository to your machine.

Options.text: To publish a repository as a template.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Clone creates a local copy that you can work with and sync later.

questions.Question: What is the usual result of a successful git commit?

Options.text: A saved snapshot of staged changes in the local repository.
A copied issue from another repository.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: A commit captures staged changes as a snapshot in repository history.

questions.Question: Which GitHub feature is used to propose changes for review before merging?

Options.reason: Pull requests propose and review changes before merge.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Pull requests are the standard way to review and merge changes on GitHub.

questions.Question: What is the difference between a local repository and a remote repository?

Options.text: Local is stored on your computer; remote is stored on GitHub or another server.
Local is public; remote is private.
Local can only contain issues; remote can only contain code.
Local always has more branches than remote.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: A local repository lives on your machine, while a remote repository is hosted elsewhere.

questions.Question: Which command initializes a new Git repository in an empty folder?

Options.reason: git init creates a new repository.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: git init creates a new local repository in the current folder.

questions.Question: Which GitHub element is best for reporting and tracking a bug?

Options.reason: Issues are used to track bugs and tasks.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Issues help track bugs, tasks, and other work items.

questions.Question: What does a repository template help you do?

Options.text: Create a new repository with prepopulated structure and files.
Options.reason: Templates speed up new repo creation.

Options.text: Convert a private repository to public.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Templates provide a starting structure for new repositories.

questions.Question: Which repository setting controls who can push or administer a repository?
questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Repository permissions determine what users can do in the repo.

questions.Question: What is the best action to preserve a file's history when changing its content in a repository?

Options.text: Edit the file and commit the change.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Editing and committing records file version history.

questions.Question: Which GitHub Desktop capability is most relevant for file-based changes?

Options.text: Visual management of commits and sync actions
Options.reason: GitHub Desktop helps manage commits and sync locally.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: GitHub Desktop provides a GUI for working with repositories and committing changes.

questions.Question: What happens when you delete a file in a Git repository and commit the change?

Options.text: The deletion is recorded in version history.
The repository loses its remote URL.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Deletes are also versioned through commits.

questions.Question: Which repository feature lets you start from a standard file and folder layout for multiple projects?
questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Templates are useful when many projects share the same starting structure.

questions.Question: Which change is typically made in repository settings rather than in code?

Options.text: Fixing a syntax error in source code
Changing a package import path in code

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Repository settings are used for branch rules, visibility, and access control.

questions.Question: What is the main purpose of forking a repository?

Options.text: Create a personal copy of someone else's repository to work independently.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: A fork is commonly used to propose changes without direct write access.

questions.Question: Which action is most appropriate after reviewing changes and approving them in a pull request?

Options.text: Convert the issue to a discussion.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: After approval, the pull request can be merged into the target branch.

questions.Question: What is the primary purpose of GitHub Actions?

Options.text: Automate workflows such as build, test, and deployment.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: GitHub Actions is used for automation and CI/CD workflows.

questions.Question: Which feature helps teams track bugs and feature requests?

Options.reason: Issues track work items and requests.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Issues are the standard tracking tool for bugs and requests.

questions.Question: Which GitHub feature supports threaded conversations around ideas or questions?
questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Discussions provide a forum-style collaboration space.

questions.Question: Which GitHub workflow is the best fit for validating code before merge?

Options.text: Create a pull request and run automated checks.
Options.reason: Pull requests are commonly paired with checks.

Options.text: Open a discussion and close it.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Pull requests often trigger checks that validate changes before merge.

questions.Question: How do labels help with issue management?

Options.text: They categorize and filter issues or pull requests.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Labels make it easier to organize and search work items.

questions.Question: What is a milestone used for in GitHub?

Options.text: Grouping related issues and pull requests toward a goal.
Options.reason: Milestones group work toward a target.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Milestones help track progress against a target or release.

questions.Question: Which item is most associated with tracking work across a team visually?

Options.reason: Projects track and organize work visually.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: GitHub Projects helps organize team work and status.

questions.Question: What is the core benefit of CI in a GitHub workflow?

Options.text: Automatically validating code changes early and often.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Continuous integration helps catch problems early.

questions.Question: Which GitHub feature is commonly used to define automated steps in response to repository events?
questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Workflows define when and how automation runs.

questions.Question: What is a code review intended to accomplish?

Options.text: Identify improvements, issues, and correctness concerns before merge.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Code review improves quality, consistency, and maintainability.

questions.Question: Which review action is most appropriate for requesting changes from an author?

Options.text: Leave a review comment and request changes.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Requesting changes is the standard way to block merge until issues are addressed.

questions.Question: What is one common reason to use branch protection rules?

Options.text: Require reviews or status checks before merging.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Branch protection can require reviews and checks before merge.

questions.Question: Which automation outcome is most associated with a successful CI pipeline?

Options.text: Build and test results are reported automatically.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: CI pipelines usually build and test code, then report status.

questions.Question: Which GitHub feature is designed for planning and tracking work at scale?

Options.reason: Projects are for planning and tracking work.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Projects help organize work into a manageable workflow.

questions.Question: What is the typical purpose of a project board column?

Options.text: Representing work status such as To do, In progress, or Done.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Project board columns help visualize progress.

questions.Question: How can issues and pull requests be integrated with GitHub Projects?

Options.text: They can be added as project items.
Options.reason: Project items can include issues and PRs.

Options.text: They can only be stored as files.
They can only be used in discussions.
They must be converted to tags.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Projects can track issues and pull requests together.

questions.Question: What is a practical use of milestones and projects together?

Options.text: Group work by release and track delivery status.
Options.reason: That is a common combined use.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Milestones can target release goals while projects track progress.

questions.Question: Which action best supports estimating future work in GitHub Projects?

Options.text: Organize issues into a prioritized view.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Prioritized views help teams plan upcoming work.

questions.Question: Which branch setting is used to reduce the risk of unstable changes reaching main?
questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Branch protection helps safeguard important branches.

questions.Question: What does Dependabot help with?
questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Dependabot supports dependency security and updates.

questions.Question: What is the purpose of organization teams?

Options.text: Manage access for groups of members.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Teams make it easier to assign permissions to groups.

questions.Question: Which action best fits organization administration?

Options.text: Adding members and assigning team-based access.
Editing code in a feature branch.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Organization admins manage members, teams, and access.

questions.Question: What is the main purpose of repository access permissions?

Options.text: Control who can view, push, or administer content.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Permissions define allowed actions for users and teams.

questions.Question: Which feature helps protect against accidental exposure of secrets?
questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Secrets are stored separately from source code.

questions.Question: Which GitHub feature is most useful for open-ended community Q&A?

Options.reason: Discussions are ideal for community Q&A.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Discussions support community interaction around questions and ideas.

questions.Question: What does it mean to contribute to an open source project through GitHub?

Options.text: Propose improvements and collaborate through issues and pull requests.
Options.reason: That is a core contribution flow.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Open source contribution commonly happens through issues and pull requests.

questions.Question: Which action is a common way to stay informed about repository activity?
questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Notifications and subscriptions help you monitor activity.

questions.Question: Why might a maintainer use a welcome or contribution-focused repository file?

Options.text: To guide contributors on how to participate.
To hide source code from collaborators.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Contributor guidance helps standardize community participation.

questions.Question: Which statement best describes a branch?
questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Branches let you develop changes independently before merging.

questions.Question: What does merging do?

Options.text: Combines changes from one branch into another.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Merge brings changes from one branch into another branch.

questions.Question: Which pull request activity is most useful for finding quality issues early?

Options.text: Reviewing the diff and leaving comments.
Options.reason: Reviewing the diff helps catch issues.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Code review helps identify issues before merge.

questions.Question: What is a good reason to use a fork instead of working directly in the main repository?

Options.text: You do not have write access and want to propose changes safely.
You need to delete the repository.
You need to create a new organization.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Forks are common when contributors do not have direct write access.

questions.Question: Which event commonly triggers a GitHub Actions workflow?

Options.text: A push or pull request update.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Workflows often run on pushes and pull requests.

questions.Question: What is the best use of a project item field such as Priority?

Options.text: To categorize and rank work for planning.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Project fields help organize and prioritize work.

questions.Question: Which setting would you use to make a repository visible only to selected people?
questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Private visibility limits who can access the repository.

questions.Question: Which GitHub feature helps people ask and answer questions around a project without creating issues?
questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Discussions are well suited to project conversations.

questions.Question: What is the purpose of pushing changes?

Options.text: Send local commits to a remote repository.
Create a new local branch only.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Push sends your local commits to the remote repository.

questions.Question: Why would you use a repository archive action?

Options.text: To mark a repository as no longer active for development.
Options.reason: Archiving preserves history and stops updates.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Archiving indicates a repository is no longer active.

questions.Question: What is the primary benefit of GitHub’s issue templates?
questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Issue templates improve the quality of submitted information.

questions.Question: Which statement about GitHub Actions is correct?

Options.text: Workflows can be reused to standardize automation.
Actions only work in private repositories.
Actions remove the need for branches.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: GitHub Actions can standardize automation across repositories.

questions.Question: How do GitHub Projects help a team most directly?

Options.text: They provide a structured view of work and progress.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Projects provide a structured way to plan and track work.

questions.Question: What is a common reason to require pull request reviews on protected branches?

Options.text: To ensure changes are examined before merge.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Reviews help ensure quality and governance before merge.

questions.Question: What is one benefit of participating in GitHub Discussions for an open source project?

Options.text: Build shared understanding around features and support questions.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Discussions help the community share context and support.

questions.Question: Which action best describes syncing local work after remote changes have been made?

Options.text: Pulling changes from the remote repository.

questions.CorrectAnswerExplanation: Pull downloads and integrates changes from the remote repository.
